gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Sign-painter brushwork with a poured-lead mass: that's Origami at a glance. Origami is best at bold single-stroke gestures, while Noto Sans Lisu is best at tidy, tightly fitted lines with open s curves.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-saira: Hollow glass-tube letters: that's Origami up top. Saira underneath is sans-serif, with rounded letters that stretch toward the top line and an open gap in every s, so the tubes get a body with room to breathe.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-sarpanch: Cord-thick curves with a lowercase like poured lead. Sarpanch, a plain sans, has an open-mouthed e and compact ascenders, so paragraphs under Origami should read smoothly and approachably, with a contemporary ease.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-sulphur-point: Brush-sign bravado with a hefty lowercase, courtesy of Origami. Both fonts draw with a steady marker-like line, and that shared hand is what makes Sulphur Point feel like Origami's quieter sibling.
